implementation_constraints: reads one JSON value from stdin, prints one line, exits 0

unresolved_intent.decision: JSON true/false (Python bool) is rejected as an invalid age even though bool is a Python int subclass
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec says age is 'an integer'; a boolean is semantically not an integer, so isinstance(age, bool) is explicitly excluded before the isinstance(age, int) check

unresolved_intent.decision: extra/unknown fields beyond first/last/age are silently ignored, not treated as an error
unresolved_intent.rationale: the spec's error list only names missing/wrong-typed first/last/age; it never says the record's field set must match exactly, so presence of extras is out of scope rather than a defect

unresolved_intent.decision: a JSON float age (e.g. 18.0) is rejected as ERROR even though its value is integral
unresolved_intent.rationale: AC-TR-05 fails on 'age is not an integer'; JSON distinguishes number kinds and Python's json module parses 18.0 as float, so strict type(age) is int semantics (via isinstance excluding bool) is used rather than a value-based integrality check

unresolved_intent.decision: use json.dumps with default separators/no indent, single-line
unresolved_intent.rationale: AC-TR-06 states only structure and values are fixed, not formatting, so the simplest compact serialization satisfies the contract without inventing an unrequested formatting guarantee
